title: The Man Who Stole A 57-Ton Army Battle Tank
sources: San Diego Police Department & California Highway Patrol Incident Reports (May 17, 1995) - Shawn Nelson stole an M60A3 Patton tank from the National Guard Armory.
The New York Times (May 19, 1995) 'Tank Rampage in San Diego Ends With Driver's Death' - The 23-minute rampage damaged 40 vehicles, traffic signals, and utilities.

lines.text: In nineteen ninety five, a man hotwired a fifty-seven-ton military battle tank with a screwdriver -
lines.caps: In 1995, | a man hotwired | a 57-ton tank | with a screwdriver -

lines.text: and drove it straight into rush-hour city traffic.
Shawn Nelson, an unemployed former soldier, casually walked into the San Diego National Guard Armory.
He climbed atop an M sixty A three Patton tank, snapped the lock, and cranked the ignition.
The massive twelve-cylinder turbo diesel roared to life.
Nelson rammed through the armory security gates and steered the steel colossus onto public avenues.
For twenty-three unbelievable minutes, he tore through suburban neighborhoods and highway State Route one sixty-three.
He crushed forty parked cars flat like tin cans, snapped utility poles, and ripped fire hydrants out of the ground,
sending geysers of water shooting thirty feet into the sky!
Police cruisers could only watch helplessly as bullets ricocheted harmlessly off the heavy armor.
Live news helicopters broadcasted the spectacle to stunned audiences across the nation.
The wild joyride only ended when the tank became wedged atop a concrete freeway divider, ending one of the craziest chases in American history.
